entries.appliesTo: licensed mental-health professionals/providers, and any individual, corporation, or entity offering therapy or psychotherapy services to the public in Rhode Island

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 40.1-5.5-3(a)(1)-(2) — 'is informed in writing of the following … (1) That artificial intelligence will be used; (2) The specific purpose of the artificial intelligence tool or system that will be used'
dutySources.consent-workflow: § 40.1-5.5-3(a) — 'unless the patient or the patient's parent, guardian or other legally authorized representative is informed in writing of the following and provides consent as defined in § 40.1-5.5-2'
dutySources.human-review: § 40.1-5.5-3(c) — 'A licensed professional or provider may not allow or otherwise use artificial intelligence to do any of the following: (1) Make independent therapeutic decisions; … (3) Determine therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans'

sources.aiTherapyRule: § 40.1-5.5-3(b) — 'An individual, corporation, or entity may not provide, advertise, or otherwise offer therapy or psychotherapy services, including through the use of Internet-based artificial intelligence, to the public in this state unless the therapy or psychotherapy services are conducted by an individual who is a licensed professional or provider' + § 40.1-5.5-2(6) — 'the licensed professional or provider maintains responsibility for clinical judgement and reasonable therapeutic oversight'
sources.consentRequired: § 40.1-5.5-3(a) — 'is informed in writing of the following and provides consent as defined in § 40.1-5.5-2'
sources.scope: § 40.1-5.5-2(10) — '"Therapy or psychotherapy services" means services provided to diagnose or treat an individual's mental health or behavioral health'
sources.enforcer: § 40.1-5.5-5(b) — 'The executive office of health and human services shall have authority to investigate any actual, alleged, or suspected violation of this chapter'; § 40.1-5.5-5(a) — 'The penalties pursuant to § 5-37.3-9 shall apply to any violation of the confidentiality provisions of this chapter'

flags: confidentiality duty with no vocabulary fit: § 40.1-5.5-4 makes all provider records and patient communications 'confidential and shall not be disclosed except as provided pursuant to the provisions of § 40.1-5-26'

penalty cross-reference (§ 5-37.3-9) applies only to 'the confidentiality provisions of this chapter'; the chapter states no penalty for violations of the use-restriction provisions (§ 40.1-5.5-3) — per rule 4 no penaltyMax coded

§ 40.1-5.5-3(a) drafting is convoluted: it conditions use of AI 'designed to simulate emotional attachment, bonding, or dependency or artificial intelligence companions' in supplementary support or therapeutic communication (where sessions are recorded/transcribed) on written notice plus consent; coded params (supervised + consent) hold on either reading

exemptions in § 40.1-5.5-5(c): religious counseling; peer support; public self-help/educational materials; FDA-reviewed-and-cleared AI tools; IRB-approved research under 21 C.F.R. Pt. 50 / 45 C.F.R. Pt. 46
EOHHS 'authorized to promulgate rules and regulations to carry out the intent of this chapter' (§ 40.1-5.5-6)
